newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 15.

text.p: Two judges facing charges: Two judges were placed in the dock on Monday to face charges in Wellington and Auckland, one accused of indecencies against children more than ten years ago and the other with fiddling his expenses while entertaining "a lady friend". Page 1.

Shipley finds nothing super in compulsory savings plan: Nothing she had seen in her various ministerial roles during the past seven years had convinced her that a compulsory retirement savings scheme was either necessary or desirable, Transport Minister Jenny Shipley said on Monday night. Page 2.

Avoidance ideas won't work -- Birch: Finance Minister Bill Birch has warned people against following Alliance suggestions for dodging payments into the proposed compulsory superannuation scheme. Page 2.
ACT expected to back scheme: ACT NZ is expected to announce today its support for the government's proposed compulsory retirement savings scheme. Page 2.

Kiwis' net worth drops -- survey: New Zealanders' net worth, excluding housing, slumped in the March quarter for the first time since 1991, according to the Westpac FPG household savings indicator made public on Monday. Page 13.
TV3 makes slightly more, says CanWest: TV3's revenues inched ahead in the nine months to May by four percent compared with the previous year, 68 percent stakeholder CanWest said on Monday. Page 13.
Bulmer set to take lion's share of cider market: British cider giant Bulmer is poised to quaff the lion's share of the New Zealand cider market. Page 13.
Plant closures loom in meat sector shakeup: An agreement between North Island meat companies on plant closures is moving closer and could be announced by the end of the week.
Govt push for 2003 World Cup: All Black coach John Hart is part of a new government initiative to get the 2003 World Cup and other big events staged in New Zealand.

Oil industry career leads to to job at FCL Forests: Fletcher Challenge has appointed Paul Fowler as head of its forests division, an executive who seems perfectly qualified to lead its energy operations.
TVNZ talking deals with regional telly rescuers: TVNZ has begun negotiating with several parties interested in buying the assets of its failed regional television stations.
Japanese cash in on our acacia: Four Japanese companies have formed a joint venture to grow acacia trees on Northland farms.
Carter Holt forecasting lift in prices: Carter Holt Harvey expects a pickup in forest product prices in the current financial year. Page 17.

South Korean bank joins NZ: South Korea's Kookmin Bank on Monday gained registration as a bank in New Zealand and it intends to target services to the Korean migrant community from an Auckland base. Page 17.
